concepts.title: Kinship and Economic Patterns of Tribal Communities

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Kinship and Economic Patterns of Tribal Communities' refers to.
questions.a: Communities organized around shared lineage and communal resource management, maintaining distinct traditions outside orthodox Varna social orders.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Kinship and Economic Patterns of Tribal Communities'.
questions.a: Tribal groups sustained autonomy through joint landholding, ancestral ties, and resource combination.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Kinship and Economic Patterns of Tribal Communities' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Beyond Big Cities: Tribal Societies (source: gess105.txt lines 15-45)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Regional Distribution of Subcontinent Tribes' refers to.
questions.a: The geographic spread of prominent indigenous lineages such as Khokhars, Gakkhars, Nagas, Cheros, Bhils, and Gonds across varied ecological zones.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Regional Distribution of Subcontinent Tribes'.
questions.a: Tribal groups dominated diverse habitats from mountainous frontiers to dense central forests.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Regional Distribution of Subcontinent Tribes' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Who were Tribal People? (source: gess105.txt lines 46-90)

concepts.title: Nomadic Pastoralism and Itinerant Service Groups

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nomadic Pastoralism and Itinerant Service Groups' refers to.
questions.a: Mobile populations moving across pastoral territories with animal herds while exchanging animal products with settled farmers for agricultural goods.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nomadic Pastoralism and Itinerant Service Groups'.
questions.a: Seasonal movement allowed pastoralists to trade animal produce for grain and crafted items.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Nomadic Pastoralism and Itinerant Service Groups' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: How Nomads and Mobile People Lived (source: gess105.txt lines 91-115)

concepts.title: The Banjara Nomad Traders and Tanda System

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Banjara Nomad Traders and Tanda System' refers to.
questions.a: A specialized merchant nomadic community organized into traveling caravans called tandas that carried grain across long distances for markets and military forces.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Banjara Nomad Traders and Tanda System'.
questions.a: Banjaras linked rural food production with urban supply chains and imperial campaigns.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Banjara Nomad Traders and Tanda System' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: How Nomads and Mobile People Lived (source: gess105.txt lines 116-150)

concepts.title: Emergence of Jatis and Caste Stratification

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Emergence of Jatis and Caste Stratification' refers to.
questions.a: Sub-caste formations arising from specialized occupational roles and the integration of tribal and artisan groups into the Varna structural framework.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Emergence of Jatis and Caste Stratification'.
questions.a: Economic specialization replaced broader varna classifications with detailed sub-caste hierarchies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Emergence of Jatis and Caste Stratification' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Changing Society: New Castes and Hierarchies (source: gess105.txt lines 151-175)

concepts.title: Rajput Lineages and Social Elevation of Tribal Chiefs

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rajput Lineages and Social Elevation of Tribal Chiefs' refers to.
questions.a: The process through which emerging warrior lineages and leading tribal families gained Kshatriya status through Brahmana endorsement and state formation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rajput Lineages and Social Elevation of Tribal Chiefs'.
questions.a: Political power enabled influential tribal rulers to transition into recognized Rajput ruling dynasties.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rajput Lineages and Social Elevation of Tribal Chiefs' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Changing Society: New Castes and Hierarchies (source: gess105.txt lines 176-200)

questions.q: Calculate the total number of villages in num_chaurasi chaurasis under the Gond administrative system. Use the method 'Gond Kingdom Village Administrative Structure'. Work with: num_chaurasi = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_villages.
questions.a: 1512 years

questions.q: Find the total village count for num_chaurasi chaurasi units in Garha Katanga. Use the method 'Gond Kingdom Village Administrative Structure'. Work with: num_chaurasi = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_villages.
questions.a: 4200 years

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gond Kingdom Village Administrative Structure' refers to.
questions.a: A hierarchical administrative framework in Gondwana dividing a kingdom into garhs, where each garh contained chaurasis of 84 villages subdivided into barhots of 12 villages.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gond Kingdom Village Administrative Structure'.
questions.a: Gond administrative hierarchy systematically grouped villages into units of 84 and 12.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Gond Kingdom Village Administrative Structure', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_villages = num_chaurasi * 84

concepts.title: Rise and Mughal Conquest of Garha Katanga

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rise and Mughal Conquest of Garha Katanga' refers to.
questions.a: The political trajectory of the prosperous central Indian Gond state that accumulated wealth through elephant trading before Mughal conquest under Asaf Khan.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rise and Mughal Conquest of Garha Katanga'.
questions.a: Garha Katanga achieved regional prominence under Rani Durgawati before facing Mughal invasion.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rise and Mughal Conquest of Garha Katanga' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: A Closer Look: The Gonds (source: gess105.txt lines 231-260)

concepts.title: Ahom State Structure and Forced Labor System

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Ahom State Structure and Forced Labor System' refers to.
questions.a: A centralized administrative organization in Assam where adult males called paiks performed mandatory state labor and served in military forces organized under clan units called khels.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ahom State Structure and Forced Labor System'.
questions.a: The Ahom state maintained infrastructure and defense through rotational compulsory public labor.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Ahom State Structure and Forced Labor System' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Ahoms (source: gess105.txt lines 261-295)

concepts.title: Ahom Cultural Evolution and Buranji Historical Chronicles

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Ahom Cultural Evolution and Buranji Historical Chronicles' refers to.
questions.a: The cultural synthesis in medieval Assam characterized by royal patronage of literature, temple land grants, and official prose historical registers written in Ahom and Assamese.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ahom Cultural Evolution and Buranji Historical Chronicles'.
questions.a: Ahom statecraft fostered sophisticated literary records called Buranjis alongside regional Hindu adoption.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Ahom Cultural Evolution and Buranji Historical Chronicles' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Ahoms (source: gess105.txt lines 296-330)
